events.note: Authored for credential-evidence epic #238 (Group E follow-up) from the contract claims and handoffs E1, E2 and E3 cited in the expectation, before any scanner was consulted; carrier existence is provider-documented, the context policy is project policy. Not an independent review.

Decided 2026-10-06 by the sole maintainer (Milo Kang, milocosmopolitan, repository owner) for credential-evidence epic #238 (Group E follow-up), on the owner's instruction of 2026-10-06 (complete redact-secret#1228, #1229 and #1230 before the next release; Cases and baselines authored maintainer-only, as in Batch 2). No dissent was raised by the maintainer; the strongest counter-argument is recorded in the dissent field. Question: A value in the hapikey query parameter is a credential whatever its shape, and does the retired era of the account key change that? Options: require a documented prefix, alphabet or length (HubSpot states none) or flag only a hyphen-grouped shape that two artifacts are consistent with; stay silent on the account key because HubSpot said it would stop working on 2022-11-30; or flag by position, whichever key kind and era. Decision: flag any value in the hapikey query parameter, both key kinds, no era exception. Reason: HubSpot documents only that the carrier exists and that the two kinds share it, and its two pages do not agree on whether a key authenticates after 2022-11-30, so the expectation rests on project policy and is not a provider rule or a fact; a credential of a retired era in a URL, log or configuration is still a redaction concern. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone under the solo-maintainer period (ADR 0020): not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). Recorded by an AI agent on the owner's instruction.
events.dissent: The pages state no value format, so a position-only rule can flag a non-secret that sits in the parameter or miss a differently placed key, and a sunset key may no longer authenticate, so flagging it may be redaction of a dead value; leaving the case a draft would claim nothing.
events.reversingEvidence: A HubSpot statement that the carrier or the key is not confidential, or of a key format that contradicts this outcome, or a second maintainer's retro-review that disputes it.
